To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 16O(e,ee‘pp)14 reaction to discrete final-state is dominated by the excitation of the $\Delta^ +$ isobar, which in turn leads to a significant enhancement of the cross section at large proton angles.

(i) the 16O(e, e’pp)14C data are consistent with the existence of short-range correlations; (ii) the 16(e, e’ pp) data are not compatible with the presence of long-range correlations; and (iii) the 16 (e,e‘pp) data are not consistent with a model in which short-range correlations are not present.

1) a good agreement between theory and experiment is achieved when including both SRC and Δ excitation in the reaction model; and 2) the spectroscopic information obtained from the 15N $(\mathrm{d},^{\mathrm{3}}\mathrm{He})^{14}$ C experiment can be used to extract reliable information on the spectroscopic amplitudes of the 14C nucleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed investigation of the 16O(e, e‘pp)14 C reaction.
the investigation of the structure of the nuclear wave function by means of electron scattering.
the study of short-range correlations (SRCs) in the nucleus, which is a fundamental ingredient in the description of the nuclear structure and dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the short-range correlations are responsible for a substantial part of the cross-section but not the entire cross-section.
the data are in agreement with a model which includes both short-range correlations and $\Delta^ +$ excitations.
short-range correlations are a necessary ingredient for an understanding of exclusive $(e, e‘pp)$ reactions, however they do not exhaustively account for all the observed phenomena.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 16O(e,ee‘pp)14 C reaction is a promising tool to extract spectroscopic information from the ground-state of 14C and to study the short-range correlations in the continuum.
short-range correlations and $\Delta^ +$ excitation are the main ingredients to describe the data.
the 16O(e, e‘pp)14 C reaction to discrete final state is dominated by the $\Delta^ +$ excitations and the short-range correlations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross-sections are sensitive to the details of the short-range correlation wave function and to the spectroscopic information of the final state.
exclusive 16O $(e,e‘pp) 14C$ processes can be used as a probe of the short-range structure of the nucleus.
the 16O(e, e‘ pp)14C reaction is an excellent tool to probe the spectroscopic information of the continuum of 14C.
